symptom: A pluggable widget's text-template property is authored and **silently dropped** — the document keeps the enumeration that says the text exists but no text, so `tooltipType: 'customText', tooltip: '…'` builds as *"'Tooltip' cannot be empty when 'Custom' type is chosen"*. The tell that makes it findable: `tooltip: 'Value {Score}'` WORKS while `tooltip: 'Plain text'` does not
cause: `setTextTemplateValue` only ever **updated an existing** TextTemplate and returned the element untouched when it was nil. A CONDITIONAL template is stored nil while its condition hides it (#574), and the Slider's tooltip is hidden under its own default `tooltipType: "value"` — so a statement that turns the condition on and writes the text in one go finds nothing to edit. `ApplyVisibilityRules` then fills the now-visible property with an EMPTY template, which is what reaches disk. The `{AttrName}` spelling escapes it only because `SetTextTemplateWithParams` **replaces** the whole template instead of editing it
file: `mdl/backend/widgetobj/builder.go` (`setTextTemplateValue`); the params gap it exposed is `mdl/executor/widget_engine.go` (`applyOperation` "texttemplate" + `resolveMapping` "TextTemplate", `BuildContext.ClientParams`)
insight: Build the envelope when the slot is nil (`updateTemplateText(BuildEmptyClientTemplate(), text)`) rather than special-casing visibility — `ApplyVisibilityRules` still runs afterwards and re-nulls a genuinely pruned property, so authored text can never survive into a slot the editor hides. **Studio Pro is the tool that localises this**: `pg_read_page` shows the stored template as a well-formed, EMPTY `Pages$ClientTemplate`, which distinguishes "no text was written" from "the template is malformed" — the BSON cannot. Two traps. Fixing the drop makes the **`{1}` spelling reachable**, and the MAPPING pass ignored `contentparams:` where the explicit-property pass has routed it since #928, so the newly-landing text hit CE0720 until both passes agreed. And **DESCRIBE still does not emit any text-template property for a pluggable widget** (`extractExplicitProperties` reads AttributeRef and PrimitiveValue only), so a tooltip survives a write and is lost on the next describe→exec — measured on the Timeline control too, i.e. every widget, tracked separately. Repro `mdl-examples/bug-tests/254-slider-custom-tooltip.mdl`. Issue #254
